tasks.short: Teach physical therapy and other health-profession students

steps.what: Prepare teaching materials for physical therapy students' learning needs
Teach students, demonstrate practice and provide individual feedback

tasks.design: Configure reusable lesson structures and approved case tags in {DOCS} or the existing {LMS}. The therapist selects and checks materials, then teaches, demonstrates, observes and gives feedback without reducing contact time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Retrieving and assembling familiar materials repeats some preparation effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native material libraries and templates can reduce assembly while keeping clinical checking.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe technique and adapting an explanation to the student.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist sees how a learner actually handles a patient and can intervene immediately.
tasks.altitude: Less material assembly with teaching and assessment responsibility intact.

reach.task: Discuss an approved case that teaches shared functional assessment principles

evidence.claim: Reusable approved materials can shorten lesson assembly while live demonstration and feedback remain; the allocation is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is therapist preparation and teaching, excluding student labour, formal qualification decisions and patient treatment time.
Therapist determines objective, learner stage, case suitability and source version in s1's retained 18.75 hours, including all field capture and checks. No ready competence label is assumed.
Only approved public or fictional cases are reused; private patient information is not transferred to teaching libraries. Missing suitable material is prepared manually.
Try native library features before custom code. Existing reuse earns no new gain. Teaching, observation and feedback retain all time.
unknowns: Current reusable materials and preparation burden
research_questions: Does material reuse reduce preparation without losing clinical accuracy or adaptation to learner needs?

already_counted.description: Material selection, capture and clinical checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=18.75+75=93.75; gross 6.25 minus 2 upkeep gives net 4.25. High requires repeated assembly; low removes only 2 hours, consumed by upkeep. Live teaching retains all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Support research and apply critically appraised findings

steps.what: Locate research sources and existing protocol material for the clinical question
Conduct or support research within the approved study protocol
Appraise research findings and determine appropriate application to practice

tasks.design: Configure saved literature searches and source-version links in {DOCS}. The therapist retains protocol-governed research work in the existing research record {OTHER}, critical appraisal and decisions about whether a finding fits clinical practice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated source retrieval can interrupt research support and appraisal.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved searches and source metadata can shorten retrieval without inventing findings.
tasks.still_hard: Protocol compliance, bias, uncertainty and translating population evidence to local clinical decisions.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist can recognise a finding that is statistically interesting but unsuitable for the patient group.
tasks.altitude: Less source hunting with research conduct and appraisal intact.

reach.task: Discuss applicability and limitations of a rehabilitation finding
reach.learn: Critical appraisal and shared practice boundaries

evidence.claim: Saved source searches can shorten literature retrieval but do not automate research conduct, validity or clinical application; the estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is a therapist's research contribution and appraisal, excluding new study authorisation, other researchers' labour and implementation of a new treatment policy. Published-source-only cases omit study activity; the allocation must be remeasured for that mix.
Therapist produces search question, terms, date limits, source identifiers and selection choices within s1's retained 10.5 hours. No structured relevance or quality score is assumed.

Research lead supplies authorised protocol and permissions through existing study governance; no participant data collection is added by this change. Missing sources are retrieved manually; incomplete findings are not summarised as settled evidence.
Test native saved searches first. Existing alerts earn no new gain. Protocol work, critical appraisal and clinical judgement keep their time; there is no automatic treatment change.
unknowns: Research duty mix, publication access and retrieval burden
Approved study processes and record permissions
research_questions: Can saved searches reduce retrieval without excluding contrary studies or obscuring protocol limitations?

already_counted.description: Search formulation, source capture and selection checks

incremental.description: Maintain search terms and source access

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=10.5+50+35=95.5; gross 4.5 minus 1.5 upkeep gives net 3. High assumes repeated source searches; low removes only 1.5 hours, offset by upkeep. Research conduct and appraisal retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in community activities and public-policy discussion

steps.what: Participate in community activities or help formulate public policy with relevant participants

tasks.design: Retain the therapist's community participation and policy contribution. Existing source material may stay in {DOCS}; the task does not establish a recurring report or consultation-administration step to remove.
tasks.previous_blocker: Community priorities and policy trade-offs require participation and understanding among people.
tasks.enabler_now: Document tools do not replace representation, local knowledge or agreement.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling unequal needs, practical resources and differing community views.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist can listen, recognise an excluded concern and explain clinical implications in public discussion.
tasks.altitude: Community contact and policy contribution time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss a shared community access concern with local participants

evidence.claim: Community and policy participation involve relationship work and judgement; no separately removable paperwork is established here.

assumptions: Boundary is therapist participation, not adoption of policy, authority of public bodies or other participants' labour.
Participants produce views and clarify priorities during retained discussion; no structured community-needs list is supplied free.
Existing reference access is baseline and native tools should be checked before future custom proposals. No public statement or commitment is automated.
No new software or maintained process is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Community activity mix and representative responsibilities
research_questions: Which participation barriers are practical or relational rather than information-retrieval problems?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Routine and contested community contributions retain participation time; no consultation paperwork baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Direct group rehabilitation activities and adapt supervision to participants' responses

tasks.design: Keep live group direction and supervision with the therapist. Programme information can remain in the clinical record {OTHER}; the task does not identify a separate scheduling or attendance-entry activity to automate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Group rehabilitation requires attention to several people with different capabilities and changing responses.
tasks.enabler_now: Record software does not provide equivalent physical supervision or clinical adaptation.
tasks.still_hard: Spotting an individual safety concern while maintaining useful activity for the group.
tasks.human_edge: The therapist notices fatigue, pain or unsafe movement and adjusts the activity immediately.
tasks.altitude: Group supervision time and professional responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate a participant's functional needs with the group programme

evidence.claim: Live group rehabilitation direction remains clinical and physical work; scheduling or reporting capabilities alone establish no supervision saving.

assumptions: Boundary is live group direction, excluding programme design, scheduling and later record drafting.
Therapist observes participant responses within retained s1; no ready structured safe-to-exercise status or automatic risk classification is assumed.
Existing programme preparation is unchanged. Review native record facilities before future custom work; no unattended supervision is introduced.
No new software or process is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Group size, participant needs and supervision requirements
research_questions: Which participant responses require immediate personal adaptation rather than more software information?

already_counted.description: Live group direction and clinical adaptation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Stable and mixed-needs groups retain live direction and observation time; no attendance paperwork is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce teaching-material assembly and source retrieval while preserving clinical education, research judgement and community and group participation.
reach: Coordinate with other therapists and clinical specialists on clear learning goals and carefully appraised rehabilitation evidence
role.ambitious_version: A therapist who uses dependable teaching and research sources while keeping attention on learners, patients and community needs.
